Start a game server

Build or extract the dedicated server for your platform. You do not need MariaDB to run a game server: accounts, room settings and game records use its local SQLite database.

macOS and Linux

From a source checkout, create a writable configuration and start an ordinary-user instance:

cp server/lineclashd.cfg.example ./lineclashd.cfg
./server/lineclashd --config ./lineclashd.cfg

From an extracted native package, use ./bin/lineclashd instead. Set explicit writable db_file and log_file paths before running it as a service.

Windows

Build the dedicated server and administration tool in an MSYS2 UCRT64 terminal:

pacman -S --needed make git mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-gcc mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-sqlite3
git clone https://github.com/kladhest-se/lineclash.git
cd lineclash
make -j4 server
./server/lineclashd.exe

SDL2 is not needed for the server. Run ./server/lineclashd-tool.exe --help for remote administration options. Keep required runtime DLLs available outside the MSYS2 environment. Press Ctrl+C in the server terminal to stop it.

Run server/lineclashd.exe from a source build or bin/lineclashd.exe from an extracted package. Defaults are stored under %APPDATA%\LineClash\Server. Use --config PATH to select another configuration.

Connect and stop

The default game port is TCP 31457. Connect the game client to localhost:31457 on the same machine, or to the server’s reachable host and port from another machine. Allow that game port through the host firewall when accepting remote players.

The separate status interface defaults to TCP 31458 and can be disabled. It is not required for a local match. See configuration and the API page before exposing status data publicly.

Stop the process before replacing its database. See server management for accounts, backups and administration. Build instructions are on Source.

Choose configuration and data paths

The server accepts --config PATH, --port PORT, --logfile PATH, --version and --help. Command-line port/log options override the configuration file; there is no --db argument. Set db_file in the configuration instead. Relative paths are resolved from the process working directory, so use absolute paths for background services.

Without --config, macOS uses ~/.lineclashd/lineclashd.cfg; Windows uses %APPDATA%\LineClash\Server\lineclashd.cfg; Linux uses /etc/lineclashd.cfg. Default database/log paths are in the same server directory on macOS/Windows and /var/lib/lineclashd/database.sqlite3 / /var/log/lineclashd.log on Linux. An ordinary Linux user should select a configuration with writable database and log paths. Use server path at the local console to check the paths actually in use.

Stop and restart safely

For a foreground instance, press Ctrl+C, or enter server shutdown in its local console. On macOS/Linux, SIGTERM also requests shutdown. To warn connected players first, use:

server shutdown 5 Planned maintenance
server shutdown cancel

The first command schedules a shutdown in five minutes; the second cancels a pending countdown. Wait for the process to exit before replacing binaries or restoring a database. An active round cannot resume after a server restart.

To restart, start the same executable with the same configuration and working directory. For a service-managed installation, stop and start the configured service rather than launching a second copy. Read configuration changes at startup; editing the file does not reload a running process. Keep writable database/log directories and avoid running the server as root.

Public discovery or a private server

Servers announce themselves to https://lineclash.example.org/api/ by default. Announcements run on a background worker and retry every 60 seconds. The website lists the connection's source IP and configured game port; allow inbound TCP on that port and forward it when hosting behind NAT. Registration does not configure your firewall or router. The separate HTTP status listener is not needed for registration.

For a private server, set public_server = off and restart. Clients can add it under Saved servers. The old public entry expires after the directory TTL, normally three minutes.

A private registration key is stored beside the SQLite database as DATABASE.directory-key. Keep it with protected backups and do not publish it. Directory downtime does not stop the game server. Self-registration provides discovery; approved operator credentials are still required by the separate statistics uploader. Registration uses the HTTP peer's public address, ignores client-supplied hosts and forwarded-address headers, and limits each source address to eight registrations.

For a game server on the directory website's own LAN, the website operator can configure automatic mapping from approved LAN addresses to the shared external IPv4. This avoids needing a public hostname. Internet clients use that public IP; internal clients can use the server's LAN IP in Saved servers, or use NAT reflection configured by the network administrator. Port forwarding is still required.

Automatic verified discovery

Updated servers detect their own external IPv4 over HTTPS, cache it for ten minutes and announce it every minute. The directory connects to the advertised game TCP port with a fresh random challenge. Only a server holding the matching directory key can produce the required HMAC response. A failed check does not publish or refresh the listing. The registration key is never sent through the public game connection.

This no longer needs local_public mapping or a shared website/game-server internet connection. public_ip can override automatic detection with a public IPv4 when routing requires it. The external game port must match the configured game port. Port forwarding remains necessary. If the directory and game server share a LAN, the directory must also be able to reach the public endpoint, usually using NAT reflection.

Clients can choose Local network to discover servers directly over UDP 31459 and connect using their LAN address, without NAT reflection for the players. Discovery is limited to the local IPv4 broadcast network and is not routed across VLANs. Allow UDP 31459 for discovery and TCP on the game port for play. lan_discovery = off disables announcements independently of public_server.

Configure a game server

Settings are read at startup. Restart after editing the configuration. Room settings saved in SQLite can override initial defaults; use room controls to update an existing room.

File format and options

One key = value per line. # starts a comment; values are unquoted. Missing keys use defaults. Empty values are ignored. Boolean switches identified below accept on/off, yes/no or 1/0; numeric flags use 1/0.

Key Default Meaning / accepted range
public_ip automatic Optional public IPv4 override; otherwise the game server detects its own address
lan_discovery on Answer local UDP discovery on port 31459
public_server on Announce this server to the official public directory; off keeps it private
server_name LineClash Name in discovery/status
port 31457 Game TCP port, 1–65535
db_file platform path above SQLite data, including accounts and room settings
log_file platform path above Append-only server log
motd Welcome to LineClash! Type /help for commands. Greeting; maximum 511 bytes
status_api on Enable public HTTP API; boolean switch
status_port 31458 HTTP TCP port; 0 disables; invalid range disables
require_registered 0 Reject new-account registration when 1
max_players_per_room 8 2–8, including bots
num_lobbies 3 1–10 rooms
global_taunts 1 Allow taunts server-wide
allow_bots on Allow hosts/admins to add bots; boolean switch
debug_auth off Legacy diagnostic toggle; authentication secrets are never logged
debug_ingame off Detailed gameplay logging; boolean switch
initiallevel 1 Starting level, 1–100
linesperlevel 2 Lines per level increase, minimum 1
levelinc 1 Levels per increase, minimum 1
averagelevels 1 Average players' levels
speciallines 1 Lines per special award, minimum 1
specialcount 1 Specials per award, minimum 0
specialcapacity 18 Inventory size, 0–64
speedup on End prolonged games with periodic garbage; boolean switch; alias speedup_enabled
speedup_delay 10 Minutes before speed-up; minimum 1
speedup_interval 60 Seconds between additions; minimum 5
speedup_lines 1 Lines per addition, 1–4
lock_delay 300 Lock delay in milliseconds, 0–500; alias lock_delay_ms
reconnect_window 15 Slot reservation during an active game, seconds, 0–120; 0 disables
garbage_system 0 0 classic, 1 guideline
garbage_targeting 0 0 all opponents, 1 random opponent, 2 focused
btb_bonus 1 Guideline back-to-back bonus, 0–4
combo_cap 4 Maximum combo bonus, 0–20
perfect_clear_bonus 10 Perfect-clear garbage, minimum 0; 0 disables
garbage_hole_style 0 0 random per line, 1 same per attack, 2 aligned
hold_enabled 1 Allow holding a piece

Room settings and bot selections persist in the database. Existing saved room preferences can override configuration defaults; use room controls or server-console help to change those rooms.

Manage a game server

Accounts and administration

New nicknames register on first connection using the client's password flow when require_registered = 0. Existing accounts must authenticate with their password. Nicknames are 1–15 printable characters without spaces or colons. Deactivated or banned accounts cannot log in.

Bootstrap an administrator from the server's local console after registering that account:

user set yournick privilege 1

Privilege levels are 1 administrator, 2 manager, 3 ordinary user. A room host can manage room settings subject to server policy. Use local-console help for commands and permission details. user set yournick active 0 disables an account; user set yournick password NEW_PASSWORD resets its password. Keep terminal history and the console restricted.

For remote administration, save a connection with the actual tool options:

./server/lineclashd-tool --add --host localhost --port 31457 --username yournick --password YOUR_PASSWORD
./server/lineclashd-tool --list
./server/lineclashd-tool --command YOUR_SAVED_ALIAS "help"

Use the alias shown by --list. --connect ALIAS opens an interactive session; --help lists options. Command-line passwords can appear in process listings and shell history. Saved password hashes are authentication credentials: restrict access to client/tool settings and database backups. Transport is plain TCP; use trusted networks or a protected tunnel for remote administration and account registration.

Exposure, backup and recovery

Both listeners bind all IPv4 interfaces. Use a firewall to restrict game/API access. Disable the API with status_api = off or status_port = 0 if public statistics are unwanted. Changing port does not automatically change status_port. An HTTPS reverse proxy can front HTTP status, but does not encrypt the separate game connection.

Stop the server before making a simple file copy of the database, or use SQLite's online backup command while running:

sqlite3 /absolute/path/database.sqlite3 ".backup '/absolute/path/backup.sqlite3'"

Keep protected, dated backups. To restore, stop the server, preserve the current database and any -wal/-shm files together, replace the database with a known-good backup, and restart. Do not mix old journal files with a restored database. Accounts, privileges, bans, room settings and statistics belong to the same database. Logs need separate rotation/retention. Ctrl+C or SIGTERM stops the server; an in-progress game is not a saved-game checkpoint.

Everyday administrator commands

The following commands use the local console syntax. Remote command availability depends on the authenticated account's privilege. Start with help for the current server's full reference.

Task Command
Check health and paths server status, server path
List rooms and users room list, user list
Inspect an account user list yournick
Announce maintenance say global Maintenance starts in five minutes
Change the greeting server motd set Welcome to our server
Disable / enable an account user set yournick active 0 / user set yournick active 1
Kick from the server user kick server yournick Reason
Ban / unban an account ban add user yournick Reason / ban remove user yournick
List bans ban list
Set a room topic room set 1 topic Casual practice
Disable room specials room set 1 specials 0
Add a practice bot bot add 1 easy
List / remove bots bot list 1, then bot remove 1 SLOT

Kicking removes a connection; banning prevents future logins until removed. A room host's /kick applies to the room and does not grant server-wide administration. Assign administrator privileges only to trusted accounts; use ordinary accounts for everyday play. Account deletion is permanent, so disabling an account is usually a better first step.

Operational checks

After starting or restarting, inspect the log for database or listener errors, run server status, and connect a client to the game port. Confirm the expected rooms and account access before inviting players. If settings seem unchanged, check server path, the process working directory and saved room settings: persisted rooms can override initial configuration defaults.

If startup fails, check config readability, database/log directory write permissions, and whether another process already owns the chosen port. Back up the database before maintenance and confirm the backup can be opened before relying on it.
